<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin ee96faa5dd5b9aeea7610b55a592e57964dbf68f && git checkout ee96faa5dd5b9aeea7610b55a592e57964dbf68f

git fetch origin 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c a97a38db05143feadc46fe4d661b6db870cc2301 && git checkout -B drift-repro 369bcbeda7bb6c2cbc8c3c3892435351506c960c && git merge --no-ff a97a38db05143feadc46fe4d661b6db870cc2301
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

The failure is `check-empty-changeset`'s DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. This PR edits three PENDING changesets (`19417-install-door-parses-manifest-id`, `19417-protocol-install-primitive-parses-manifest-id`, `19576-install-local-id-gate`), and only in their verbatim quotes of the refusal sentence this PR changes. Under `landing-operations.md` the confirmation is a same-head at-tier contract-review PASS record that names each corrected note and judges each rewritten sentence. That review is running now, and its record will be posted on this PR. ⛔ No `skip-changeset`, ⛔ no re-run, ⛔ no gate change. `Check Changeset` is not a required context, so the red rides into the queue under the SKILL.md three conditions once the record is in. If the record FAILs a rewrite, the PR goes back to the dev for a patch round.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 66/66 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a97a38db05143feadc46fe4d661b6db870cc2301`

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Ruling items 1–5 vs diff.**
   - Item 1: `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` is exactly `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)+$/`. An exhaustive probe over every string of length ≤7 on the alphabet `ab19-._` finds 0 ids the old pattern accepted and the new refuses, so the widening is purely additive.
   - Item 2: the refusal sentence and the `id` TSDoc carry the ruling's wording verbatim; the docblock line 「Each segment starts with a letter」 is gone; `MANIFEST_ID_EXAMPLES` is unchanged.
   - Item 3: one `ACCEPTED` / `REFUSED` table. `com.example.2app` and `com.163.crm` are accepted and parse to themselves. `com.example.-app`, `com.example.my_app` and `Com.Example.App` are refused with `invalid_format` and the declaration's own sentence. `PackageSchema.manifestId` is judged on the same table.
   - Item 4: no hunk touches `manifest.namespace` or `namespace-prefix.ts`.
   - Item 5: `@objectstack/spec: minor`.
   - One divergence: the ruling wrote `Clause-②: no`, while the PR and changeset declare `yes (widening)`. Under the canonical reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) the value answers whether the card widens the accept set, and this diff does, so the PR's spelling is the correct one. Non-blocking.
2. **Accept set and consumers.** Probed:
   - Refused: `-.a`, `a.-`, `com.example.-app`; `123` and `2app` (single segment); `com..app`, `.com.app`, `com.app.`; underscores; upper case.
   - Accepted: `123.456`, `com.example.123`, `9foo.bar`, `local.2024-app`.
   - Both doors share the constant (`package.zod.ts:172-174`).
   - No consumer breaks. The runtime map keys by the string. `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` gives `com.163.crm` → `crm` and `com.example.123` → `null` (namespace left unset). `slugify` in `publish.ts` yields `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` or `'app'`, so every derived `local.` id parses. Both scaffolders still prefix `app-`.
   - Residual, carried from the ruling's own wording: the sentence says 「inner hyphens」 while the pattern admits a trailing hyphen. The sentence over-refuses, so no author following it is refused. Non-blocking.
3. **Prose truth at head.** Every sentence checked is true: the refusal sentence, the TSDoc, migration entry 18 (unreleased) and the `registry.ts` regeneration, the `publish.ts` docblocks, and the new changeset. One sentence in `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` is imprecise: it lists three remedies where each refusable source prints a subset. Every listed remedy works, so no author is misdirected. Non-blocking.
4. **DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** `Check Changeset` (both runs) exits 1, with one annotation per file under the foreign-changeset rule, naming exactly three notes:
   - `.changeset/19417-install-door-parses-manifest-id.md`
   - `.changeset/19417-protocol-install-primitive-parses-manifest-id.md`
   - `.changeset/19576-install-local-id-gate.md`

   In each note the single change is inside the quoted refusal block. It was `… — lowercase dot-separated segments; hyphens allowed inside a segment, underscores are not. Did you mean '…'?` and is now `… — lowercase dot-separated segments of letters, digits and inner hyphens; a segment may not open with a hyphen; underscores are not admitted. Did you mean '…'?` (for `pkg-a` → `com.example.pkg-a`, `com.example.my_erp` → `com.example.my-erp`, and `late-app` → `com.example.late-app` respectively).

   `manifestIdRefusal` was reconstructed from the head source: each quoted block, unwrapped, equals the head output byte for byte. Each rewrite is TRUE and stays inside the quote, and no other line of the three notes moved. Their 「If you are refused」 paraphrase states a subset of the widened rule and remains true. **Confirmed as the deliberate-correction class; do not restore from base.**
5. **Repo-wide pins.** The old regex literal appears nowhere at head, generated reference docs included. No remaining test asserts a digit-led id as refused. Stale comments still state the retired clause (`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:99`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/rewrite-identity.ts:113`, `rewrite-identity.test.ts:156`); they are disclosed in the PR, and their output pins hold. Non-blocking.

### ② Semver level
`minor` is right. The 2026-09-04 ruling (batch #35, #15294) makes a purely additive widening of a published accept set at least `minor`. All packages sit in one `fixed` group, so metadata-protocol, cloud-connection and cli (tests plus a comment-only docblock) need no note of their own. `content/docs` releases nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Scaffolder `app-` prefix: out of scope. The output stays legal; the two comments state a retired rule.
- `os package publish` derived-source remedy arms: verified unreachable. Dead but harmless.
- objectui `PACKAGE_ID_RE` (`packages-io.ts:244`): out of scope for this card. It does not import the spec constant, and it is now stricter than the server on `9foo.bar`. Nothing reaches the server wrongly. It deserves its own objectui card.
- `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` digit strip: pre-existing code, first reachable on a legal id through this widening. The ruling accepted it.
- Studio plugin id: a different key with its own pattern, correctly untouched.
